policy.last_change: 4 Mar 2026 (-25bp, eff. 5 Mar); held 9 Apr, 6 May and 2 Jun

policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 25 Jun close (1x4 3.82, 3x6 3.82, 6x9 3.85, 9x12 3.88 vs WIBOR 3M 3.85) price roughly 5bp of NBP hikes within 12 months. The MPC held at 3.75% on 2 Jun (May CPI eased mainly on food; decisions stay data-dependent); Glapiński (3 Jun): lower May CPI cuts the hike odds, rates are high enough and there is no reason to change or even discuss them. Duda (18 Jun): stable rates the base case, little room for cuts; the May voting record (18 Jun) shows Tyrowicz's +100bp motion rejected again. May CPI 3.1% (final, 15 Jun; flash 29 May, 3.7% expected); core 3.1% (16 Jun). Standard fuel excise is back from 15 Jun; VAT 8% and price caps run to 30 June, with a VAT decision due 'shortly' (Tusk, 16 Jun).
policy.risk_text: FRAs no longer price NBP hikes (PKO, 25 Jun) and Brent is back at pre-war levels (~$73); risks: a renewed Gulf flare-up, the end of the fuel package in July lifting CPI, the July MPC with its projection, and Q3 supply with a 6.5-7% deficit.

macro.projection_text: NBP March projection (4 Mar; data to 19 Feb, war excluded): CPI 50% bands 1.6-2.9% (2026), 1.1-3.7% (2027); central path 2.3% / 2.4% / 2.3% (2026-28), GDP 3.9% in 2026; IMF (14 Apr): 2026 CPI 3.3%; EC (21 May): GDP 3.5% in 2026; OECD (June outlook): CPI 3.7% in 2026, no cuts before Q2 2027; Fitch (8 Jun): GDP 3.3%, NBP flat at 3.75% to year-end; World Bank (11 Jun): GDP 3.1% / 2.6%; NBP survey of economists (24 Jun): CPI 3.0% / 2.9% (2026-27). The July projection is the next marker.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit 7.3% of GDP (GUS EDP, 22 Apr), debt 59.7%; 2026 deficit cap PLN 271.7bn; budget deficit after May PLN 108.2bn (~40% of the limit, 15 Jun); the government's assumptions put the 2026 deficit at ~6.8% of GDP; EC (21 May): 6.5%, debt 64.5%; EKF consensus (2 Jun): 6.9%; EDP debt 61.6% of GDP at end-Q1 (10 Jun); 2027 budget path (9 Jun): GDP 3.1%, CPI 2.5%; the Senate amended the windfall tax (25 Jun); fuel package (VAT 8%, price caps) to 30 June, standard excise back from 15 June.
macro.fiscal_risk_text: 2026 needs ~62% (MoF, 24 Jun) financed; budget accounts PLN 208.3bn at end-May (MoF, 8 Jun); 3 Jun switch (MoF database): PLN 11.63bn sold (demand 12.84bn) vs 10.90bn bought back (PS0527 7.42bn), net +0.73bn; OK0129 4.812%, PS0731 5.269%, DS0436 5.703%; BGK priced EUR 2bn of FPC bonds (2 Jun). S&P A-/stable (8 May); Scope A negative (15 May); Fitch A- negative - its CEO (23 Jun, reported 24 Jun) calls public finances the main rating risk; Moody's A2 negative.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP held at 3.75% on 2 Jun; May CPI 3.1% y/y; Q1 GDP 3.5% y/y (second estimate). Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 25 Jun: the 8th KPO request is worth PLN 33.8bn. The Senate amended the windfall tax (cap on the amount). Brent fell to ~$73 as Hormuz traffic normalised; Millennium: rates -6-11bp despite the auction. PKO's Budzicki: no NBP hikes priced any more, stable rates 2026-27 the base case; Tuesday's flash CPI is seen near target. EUR/PLN ~4.29, a 3-month low for PLN. DS0436 5.33%. Abroad: US May PCE 4.1% (core 3.4%) was in line or softer, Q1 GDP revised to 2.1%, claims 215k; UST10 fell below 4.40% (seven-week low) as futures trimmed multi-hike bets (FedWatch ~66% for a hike by September). EU states gave final approval to the EU-US tariff deal before 4 July. A projectile hit a ship off Oman and the IRGC warned off non-Iranian routes; Brent ~$73-75. HU10 near 2022 lows; Bund 2.86%.

calendar.plan_text: MoF June plan (29 May): one switch on 3 Jun (settles 8 Jun; buys back DS0726, PS1026, WZ1126, OK0127, PS0527) and sale auctions on 17 and 24 Jun (PLN 6-12bn each) in OK0129, NZ0331, PS0731, DS0436 and NZ0936; no T-bills; ~56% of 2026 needs financed. 3 Jun switch (MoF database): PLN 11.63bn sold (demand 12.84bn) vs 10.90bn bought back (PS0527 7.42bn), net +0.73bn; OK0129 4.812%, PS0731 5.269%, DS0436 5.703%. 17 Jun sale: PLN 12.00bn vs 18.27bn demand (cover 1.52) plus 0.79bn; OK0129 4.399%, PS0731 4.918%, DS1030 4.711%, DS0436 5.416%. 24 Jun sale: PLN 12.00bn vs 15.42bn demand (cover 1.28) plus 1.32bn; OK0129 4.396%, PS0731 4.911%, DS1035 5.334%, DS0436 5.417%. BGK switch (18 Jun): PLN 1.35bn of FPC sold (demand 2.11bn) vs 1.44bn of FPC0427 bought back.
calendar.timing_text: The Aug 2025-Feb 2026 pattern (auction-day close the cheapest point of the week) comes from a rally regime; March's sell-off broke it and April's auction days cheapened on average. June supply is done (PLN 24.0bn sold in two sales plus 2.11bn additional, and the 3 Jun switch); the July/Q3 plan is due at end-June. Next MPC in July, with the NBP projection: a hold is expected. Covers: 1.52 (17 Jun), 1.28 (24 Jun) vs 1.25-1.33 in May.

facts.core_text: Regime: oil back to pre-war levels (~$73) as Hormuz traffic normalises; the NBP held at 3.75% on 2 Jun while FRAs price roughly 5bp of NBP hikes; the ECB hiked to 2.25% on 11 Jun with one more hike priced, the Fed signals a 2026 hike in its dots, the BoE held 7-2, the CNB hiked to 3.75% and the MNB cut to 6.00%. Poland's 5Y CDS was 50bp and the 10Y spread to Bunds 241bp on benchmark bonds (Erste, 25 Jun close). US PCE 4.1%; UST10 below 4.40% (25 Jun).

quasi_takeaways: FPC fixed lines trade ~{lo}-{hi}bp over the POLGB curve (average {avg}bp); widest ASW {widest} at {widest_asw}bp. Same State Treasury guarantee as POLGBs.
Best pickup: {best} ({best_sp}bp vs POLGB). For buy-and-hold books the guarantee makes the pickup attractive; liquidity is the cost (Pekao became BGK market maker on 13 Nov 2025).
Supply: BGK's first FPC switch (18 Jun): PLN 1.35bn sold (demand 2.11bn) vs 1.44bn of FPC0427 bought back (net about -0.09bn); Q3 issuance to prefund 2027 needs.
Use auctions, not Catalyst: trades are small retail lots and some lines go weeks without a print.
